author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dr. Jonathan Marsh believes the future of Alzheimer’s care will be shaped by prevention. In his talk, Dr. Marsh explores advances that could change Alzheimer’s from a disease of aging into a disease that can be prevented. From GLP-1 medications and monoclonal antibodies currently in use, to vaccines and new inhaled therapies now in development, these breakthroughs raise a striking possibility: that within a decade, Alzheimer’s may no longer define the future for millions. 

After training at Clemson University and earning his MD at the Medical University of South Carolina, where Dr. Jonathan Marsh also completed his Internal Medicine residency, he moved to Naples, Florida in 2012 and became a serial entrepreneur in healthcare. He founded Naples Concierge Health to move beyond the constraints of traditional fee-for-service models, creating space for innovation, patient education, and preventive care. Today, he continues to lead Naples Concierge Health, guided by the belief that science
title: Could we eradicate Alzheimer's disease? | Jonathan Marsh | TEDxNaples

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when being strong becomes something we feel compelled to perform?

This talk explores the hidden emotional cost of always appearing confident, composed and unaffected. It examines how suppressing fear, sadness and vulnerability can prevent us from understanding ourselves and seeking the support we need.

The talk challenges the belief that strength means hiding our struggles. Instead, it presents true courage as the willingness to acknowledge our emotions, face difficult moments honestly and move forward with self-awareness and resilience. Adithyan is a curious and driven higher secondary student who enjoys exploring ideas that challenge the way people think. While preparing for his board examinations, he also pursues his passion for music, digital content creation, and building realistic DIY models from scratch. A firm believer in stepping beyond his comfort zone, he sees every new opportunity as a chance to learn and grow.
Taking the TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth
title: The Hidden Cost of Being Strong | Adithyan J V | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Kalaripayattu is often viewed simply as an ancient martial art, but its significance extends far beyond combat.

This talk explores Kalaripayattu as a living expression of Kerala’s cultural heritage—one that brings together movement, discipline, awareness, courage and a deep connection between body and mind. It reflects on how traditions passed down through generations can continue to hold meaning in a rapidly changing world.

By looking beyond the physical techniques of Kalaripayattu, the talk invites us to recognise the values, identity and wisdom embedded within our heritage, and to consider how preserving the past can also shape the way we become in the future. Aaryasree A A is a 17-year-old student of Humanities, youth speaker, writer, and accomplished leader from India. A decorated Model United Nations delegate and debater, she is passionate about geopolitics, with a particular interest in economics and global affairs.
Beyond the debate floor, Aaryasree expresses her ideas throu
title: More Than a Martial Art | Aaryasree A A | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Good leadership is often associated with planning, efficiency and achieving results. But technical knowledge and logical thinking alone are not enough to guide people effectively.

This talk explores the balance between logic and emotion, management and empathy, and results and relationships. It shows how understanding different perspectives, communicating with compassion and valuing diverse strengths can transform the way teams work together.

True leadership is not about choosing between clarity and compassion. It is about bringing both together to create meaningful and lasting impact. An analytical high school student pursuing law, Ishaan Kiran Mithra loves finding the unexpected connections between technology, leadership, and human behavior. From coding to public speaking, they have always operated at the intersection of logic and structure. However, through their hands-on experiences managing school events and collaborative projects, they realized that true impact requires more t
title: Leading Beyond Logic | Ishaan Kiran Mithra | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Femininity is often misunderstood as weakness or confined within limiting stereotypes.

This talk challenges those assumptions and explores how femininity can be a source of confidence, courage and strength. It examines the expectations placed on girls and women and the pressure to change themselves in order to be respected or considered powerful.

The talk encourages every girl to reject restrictive labels, embrace her identity with pride and recognise that equality does not require becoming less feminine—it requires society to stop treating femininity as something lesser. Nandhana Vinod is a Class 10 student at Chinmaya Vidyalaya, Kollam, with a deep passion for writing, public speaking, and expressing ideas that inspire meaningful conversations. She believes that words have the power to challenge perspectives and spark positive change.

Passionate about feminism and gender equality, Nandhana hopes to encourage young people to embrace femininity with confidence and redefine it as a
title: Femininity Is Strength | Nandhana Vinod | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

description:
What happens when two people with very different scrolling habits exchange their digital routines?

Through a simple social experiment, this talk explores how everyday scrolling can quietly influence attention, emotions, behaviour and the way we experience life. It examines the difference between using technology consciously and allowing an automatic habit to control our time and thoughts.

The talk encourages us to become more aware of what we consume online and to transform mindless scrolling into intentional digital engagement. Devangana is a curious learner with a passion for classical dance, public speaking, and debate. She loves exploring new ideas and challenging perspectives, believing that every conversation has the power to transform the way we think. Driven by a passion for trying new things, Devangana takes on a unique social experiment: swapping the scrolling habits of an addictive scroller and a passive scroller. title: The Scroll Swap | Devangana A R | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Small moments often pass unnoticed, yet a word of encouragement, thoughtful advice or simple act of kindness can alter the course of a person’s life.

This talk explores the ripple effect of everyday interactions and how their influence may continue far beyond what we can immediately see. It reminds us that meaningful change does not always begin with grand gestures; sometimes, it begins with choosing to notice, support and uplift another person. Aarushi Pramod is a 14-year-old student of Class IX at Chinmaya Vidyalaya Vazhuthacaud who believes that the smallest moments often create the biggest changes.
A creative thinker with a passion for painting, drawing, writing, reading and storytelling, she enjoys observing people and finding meaning in everyday experiences.
Beyond academics, Aarushi is a Kata Gold Medalist in Karate, a member of her school's Kho-Kho and Dance teams, and an enthusiastic participant in art, literary and exhibition events. Through her TEDx Chinmaya Vidyalaya Attu
title: Small Moments, Big Changes | Aarushi Pramod B | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Stories do more than entertain us. They influence how we understand the world, interpret our experiences and imagine our possibilities.

This talk explores how the narratives around us—and the stories we repeatedly tell ourselves—can shape our thoughts, decisions, behaviour and identity. Some stories encourage us to grow, while others quietly limit what we believe is possible.

By becoming more conscious of the stories guiding our lives, we can question inherited assumptions, rewrite limiting narratives and take a more active role in shaping who we become. Abhilash Sudheesh is a filmmaker, storyteller, and a creative strategist whose work explores the intersection of storytelling, branding, and human behaviour.

He is the Founder and Creative Head of 11th Hour Productions — a Kerala-based media production house. Throughout his career, he has led creative teams working with some of the country's leading brands, multinational companies, and institutions, crafting stories that connect wi
title: The Stories We Become | Abhilash Sudheesh | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are often told that success begins with knowing exactly who we are and what we want. Lyuboslav Dimitrov challenges this assumption by exploring how fixed definitions can limit curiosity, growth and unexpected possibilities. Drawing on his experience with young people and mentors, he argues that uncertainty is not necessarily a weakness—it can be the space in which new directions, identities and ambitions emerge.
 Lyuboslav Dimitrov is a partner and Country Lead at Mentor the Young Bulgaria, where he helps build communities that connect ambitious young people with experienced mentors. Through the programme, participants work toward entrepreneurial, professional and personal goals. Alongside his work in mentorship and community-building, Lyuboslav develops independent projects in film and television. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Who are we when we step outside the roles assigned to us? Drawing on her experiences in journalism and theatre, Viktoria Kostova explores identity as something fluid, shaped by the stories we tell, the characters we inhabit and the expectations of others. Her talk invites us to look beyond labels and search for the more honest, human voice beneath them.
 Viktoria Kostova is a second-year Journalism student at New Bulgarian University, where she combines her interests in media, culture and personal stories. She graduated from the Plovdiv Language School, where she developed her passion for languages, writing and communication. Viktoria also has a long-standing interest in theatre, which has taught her how to express ideas, understand an audience and search for the emotion behind words. This connection between journalism and the stage inspires her to look for the human and authentic perspective in every story. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but indep
title: Who Am I? | Viktoria Kostova | TEDxNBU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How much of today do we lose while waiting for tomorrow? Ana-Maria Papazova reflects on the pressure to follow a fixed plan and become a single, predetermined version of ourselves. Drawing on her own changing aspirations, she invites us to see life as a palette of possibilities, to remain open to change and to find meaning in the present instead of constantly postponing it for an imagined future.
 Ana-Maria Papazova is a second-year Journalism student at New Bulgarian University. A graduate of the Vasil Levski Sports School, she once believed that her future would remain entirely connected to rhythmic gymnastics. Over time, she discovered that life is not a single predetermined path but a palette of possibilities. She believes that identity is a constantly evolving story and tries to find meaning in the present rather than limiting herself to one permanent version of who she should become. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized
title: Today” and “Tomorrow | Ana-Maria Papazova | TEDxNBU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A name may seem like a simple label, but it can carry history, meaning, expectations and a deeply personal story.

Drawing from her own experiences, Jasmita Yasothamani Rukmoni explores how names influence identity, confidence and the way we understand ourselves. She invites us to look beyond the letters and sounds of a name and discover the stories, values and sense of belonging it can represent.

This talk encourages us to embrace the uniqueness of our names and recognise that understanding where we come from can help shape who we choose to become. Jasmita is a curious learner with a passion for science, music, and uncovering the extraordinary in everyday life. She is fascinated by the power of words and believes that even something as simple as a name can shape identity, confidence, and purpose.
Drawing from her own journey, Jasmita takes the TEDx stage to explore how names are more than labels—they carry stories, meaning, and the potential to influence who we become. Through her t
title: MORE THAN A NAME | Jasmita Yasothamani Rukmoni | TEDxChinmaya Vidyalaya Attukal Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a humorous and deeply personal story, Aleksandar Kadiev revisits the unexpected turns, mistakes and uncomfortable moments that have shaped his life. Moving between self-irony and reflection, he shows how getting lost does not necessarily mean that we have failed—sometimes it simply means that we need to change the address we are trying to reach. A talk about authenticity, self-acceptance and the courage to begin again.
 Aleksandar Kadiev is a Bulgarian theatre, film and television actor and one of the country’s most recognisable television hosts. He graduated in Drama Acting from the National Academy for Theatre and Film Arts in Sofia. His career includes numerous stage productions, film and television roles, as well as many years of live broadcasting. Known for his spontaneous humour and openness, Aleksandar turns personal experiences into engaging stories about authenticity, vulnerability and the courage to remain true to oneself. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Who teaches us to believe that we are not good enough? Drawing on her personal and entrepreneurial journey, Ina Gavazova explores how criticism, imposed expectations and other people’s definitions of success can shape our self-image. Her talk is an invitation to question these inherited beliefs, reclaim creative confidence and build a path based on purpose rather than fear.
 Ina Gavazova is a creative entrepreneur, animation art director and founder of Kashu Company, a boutique studio specialising in visual storytelling and 2D animation. In 2024, she was recognised in the Forbes Bulgaria 30 Under 30 selection. She is also an active mentor and animation educator. Ina is currently expanding Kashu into a full-service creative agency while developing an international learning platform for young creative professionals. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

After spending hours assembling a chair, Ivet Yaneva discovers that she has been following the wrong instructions. This everyday mistake leads to a larger realization: sometimes the problem is not that we are incapable, but that we are following a path that was never meant for us.
 Ivet Yaneva is a Public Relations student at New Bulgarian University with an interest in communication and personal and corporate image-building. She has delivered educational talks to students on human trafficking, psychoactive substances and personal responsibility. Her professional experience includes working as a junior manager at OTTO.Artists, where she coordinated teams and contributed to communication strategies and social media development. She believes that choosing a meaningful direction sometimes requires the courage to leave behind a path that only appears to be the right one. She explores how learning goes beyond grades, exams, and the classroom, highlighting the importance of developing critical thinking, confidence, values, and the skills needed to face real-life challenges. Through a student’s perspective, María José invites us to rethink education as an experience that not only prepares us for the future, but also shapes who we become. As part of the Hontanar community, María José continues to develop her academic and personal skills while embracing opportunities that allow her to learn, grow, and share her ideas with others. author: TEDx Talks
description:
みなさんのスマートフォンに表示される写真は、いったいどのようにしてここまで届いたのでしょうか。
この問いについて一度でも考えてみたことがありますか。
私たちの手元に届く膨大な情報は、それを記録し、守り、伝えてきた人々の意思と営みの上に成り立っています。
現代の情報社会にあふれる大量のデータに翻弄されるのではなく、それらをより良い未来のために活かすには、情報がどのように生まれ、保存され、受け継がれてきたのか、その「プロセス」に目を向ける必要があります。
嘉村氏はこのtalkを通して、自身の専門分野であるデジタルアーカイブの観点から、私たちが情報とどのように向き合うべきか、その手がかりを示します。

How did the photos displayed on your smartphone get there? Have you ever stopped to think about it? 
The vast amount of information we receive is built upon the intentions and efforts of those who have recorded, protected, and passed it on.
  Rather than being swept away by the flood of data in today’s information society, we need to turn our attention to the process by which information is created, preserved, and inherited if we are to use it to build a better future.

He advocates for the importance of "working with feeling" and finding genuine joy even in the exhaustion that comes from doing what you are passionate about. Reminding the audience that while earning a living is a reality, massive wealth is not a prerequisite for a fulfilling life, he encourages everyone to pursue a path that resonates with their inner self. How does a fleeting moment become a lasting visual story? Exploring the creative process behind capturing a single frame, Levent Özdemir explains how translating complex ideas into powerful imagery always begins with an initial spark of inspiration. Exploring the importance of perseverance and staying true to one's path, Emre Nalbantoğlu shares a powerful message about facing reality with courage. He reminds us not to be afraid of moving forward, emphasizing that true change requires confronting difficult situations head-on rather than waiting for things to change on their own. By highlighting that a sudden spark or a profound breakthrough can happen at any moment, he encourages us to never give up on our journey. Sometimes expressing our deepest emotions and finding our authentic voice starts with a single note a brave beginning. Exploring the connection between music, raw passion, and authenticity, musician Emre Nalbantoğlu shares his personal journey of turning an initial spark of inspiration into a musical career. Prof. Dr. Arzu Tektaş completed her undergraduate studies in Industrial Engineering at Boğaziçi University and earned her PhD in operations management. She is currently a Professor of Quantitative Decision Methods in the Department of International Trade at Boğaziçi University, where she also serves as the Director of the School of Applied Sciences and the Vice Director of the Innovation Center. Her academic research focuses on productivity analysis, supply chain management, innovative business models, and innovative approaches in agriculture. description:
Exploring the overwhelming pace of modern life driven by rapid technological advancements, Ahmet Canbaz discusses how we risk getting lost in a flood of imposed living standards. He emphasizes that the picture imposed on us by the digital age turns us into mere extras in our own lives, rather than the leading roles. Highlighting the danger of becoming alienated from our true selves in this constant rush, he urges the audience to step back and reconnect with their authentic identities amidst the chaos. Stepping behind the scenes of memorable productions, Ahmet Canbaz explores the transformative power of documentary filmmaking. He shares his perspective as a visual storyteller, discussing what it takes to bring mind-opening stories to the screen and how these narratives leave a lasting mark on our collective memory.

Through inspiring stories ranging from a math teacher's appreciation of a uniquely "beautiful" solution to the profound personal growth students experience at project camps she illustrates how students can begin a journey with anxiety and nervousness, only to return with a completely new vision and a transformed sense of self. Dr. Meral Topal is an educational administrator and researcher who pioneers the development of an innovation and entrepreneurship culture in education. Adding depth to the field through her academic work, Dr. Topal has conducted research across a wide range of topics, including higher education to employment transitions, school development strategies, and the accreditation processes of education faculties. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this powerful and deeply personal talk, pharmaceutical industry leader Hitesh Upreti explores one of Africa's most important questions: What happens when a nation can produce something, but cannot produce it without someone else's knowledge, technology, or supply chain?

For more than 30 years, Hitesh has worked across the pharmaceutical industry, including nearly two decades across Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Nigeria. Again and again, he was brought into organisations because he knew how to solve difficult problems.

But he came to realise that being the person who always had to be brought in was not the ultimate measure of success.

The real achievement was making sure he was no longer needed.
Hitesh shares the story of a pharmaceutical factory in Tanzania where he inherited a leadership team dominated by expatriates. When he left, six critical leadership positions were held by Tanzanians.

For him, that was more significant than the company's profits or awards.

description: Exploring how we can transform our moments of sadness and adversity into a “spark”of inspiration, Afra discusses the power of channeling negative experiences into art. She shares her personal journey of turning life’s setbacks into creative success, highlighting that our most difficult moments can be the exact catalyst needed to discover a new version of ourselves and produce original, authentic work. Elif Afra Kılıç, known by her stage name Afra, is a young musician who blends pop and alternative music, performing her own lyrics and compositions. Starting her music production at an early age, the artist stepped into her professional career by deciding to share the works she had kept to herself for a long time on digital platforms. She reached millions of listeners in a short time with songs like "Yasemen" and "Kafam Leyla," with both lyrics and music belonging entirely to her. author: TEDx Talks
description:
For thousands of years, the rules of money have been written by people most of us were never invited to the room to meet.

But what happens when we get to pick up the pen?

In this provocative and visionary talk, Ifelade Ayodele takes us on a journey through the evolution of money—from systems built around absolute ownership to a new era of fractional stakes, shared participation, and radically expanded access.

He argues that money has never been static. It has continually evolved as humanity found new ways to exchange value. And now, we are approaching what may be the sixth great rewrite of money.

This time, something is different.

The opportunity is not simply to participate in a financial system designed elsewhere. It is to help shape what comes next.

Drawing from his experience across banking, venture investing, global financial institutions, and financial technology, Ifelade explores how mobile technology transformed Africa's relationship with financial access—and why the con
title: The future of money is being written right now | Ifelade Ayodele | TEDxMaitama

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Have you ever fixed one problem—only to create three new ones?

What if the problem isn't the problem?

In this insightful and eye-opening talk, Fidelis Akpoghiran introduces us to the power of systems thinking: a way of seeing the invisible connections, feedback loops, and relationships that shape the outcomes we experience every day.

We often see potholes, flooding, rising healthcare challenges, poor electricity supply, food insecurity, or organisational failures as isolated problems. But what happens when we stop looking at individual events and start looking at the system producing them?

Fidelis shows us why bigger drains alone cannot solve urban flooding, why treating millions of malaria cases does not necessarily solve the conditions that keep producing them, and why building more power plants is only part of the solution to reliable electricity.

The lesson is simple but profound:
Every outcome is perfectly designed by the system that produced it.

title: What If the Problem Isn’t the Problem? | Fidelis Akpoghiran | TEDxMaitama

description:
How many opportunities have you rejected before anyone else had the chance to say no?

You decided you weren't experienced enough.

Not connected enough.
Not qualified enough.
Not the kind of person who belonged in that room.

Nobody rejected you.
You rejected yourself.

In this powerful and deeply personal talk, Olufunsho Peters challenges us to examine the invisible limits that shape our lives—not the limits imposed by reality, but the assumptions we inherit, repeat, and eventually mistake for truth.

From teaching himself technology at fourteen to building a career spanning more than two decades of digital transformation, Olufunsho has built his life around a deceptively simple question:

“Can it be done?”

His journey takes him from secretly learning on his brother's computer, to walking across Lagos to visit a Mercedes-Benz showroom he could not afford, to surviving a devastating business crisis that left his company with more than ₦50 million in negative exposure.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We love heroes.

The visionary founder. The fearless leader. The person who sees what nobody else sees and changes everything.

But what if we have been looking at progress the wrong way?

In this powerful and thought-provoking talk, Fifehan Osikanlu challenges our obsession with individual brilliance and makes the case for a different model of progress: ecosystems beat heroes.

Across Africa, extraordinary entrepreneurs, creatives, innovators, and changemakers are building remarkable things. Yet too many are forced to struggle alone—searching for capital, partnerships, mentorship, visibility, talent, and the networks needed to turn great ideas into lasting impact.

Fifehan argues that the greatest breakthroughs rarely happen because one person is exceptional. They happen when the right people, resources, institutions, capital, and opportunities connect at the right time.

author: TEDx Talks
description: Is the future truly unwritten, or are we simply unable to see the story unfolding? In this thought-provoking talk, Beril Mardin explores the science and philosophy of free will, drawing on neuroscience, determinism, and evolution to challenge our understanding of choice. She argues that while we cannot control every force shaping our lives, our greatest strength lies in our ability to adapt, steer, and grow within uncertainty. After more than 20 years of experience in various fields of advertising and marketing communications ranging from copywriting and creative directing to strategic planning and client relations management, Beril Mardin decided to make a shift in her career and turned to education. A proud graduate of UAA 90’, she holds a BA from Boğaziçi University and an MA from Indiana University, Bloomington in English Language and Literature. title: Out damned spot, out I say! | Beril Mardin | TEDxUAA Youth

description: Psychology of hanging out with machines After sneaking away from a prairie farm, Shane’s early career was as an entrepreneur in North America and Europe focused on robotics and connected devices. He spent a decade as an innovation consultant for Fortune 500 clients, combining his technical knowledge with a natural knack for business strategy. Shane is currently an Assistant Professor at McMaster University researching why we treat robots, AI, and other social machines like people. He is a prolific writer on technology and frequently gives talks on robotics, AI, design thinking, and the future of technology in society. Shane is a former Vanier scholar who holds a PhD in robotics with a specialization in psychology from the University of Toronto, a MBA in technology and innovation from the Ted Rogers School of Management, and a B. Importance of science communication Dr. Raha is an Associate Professor in the Department of Pediatrics at McMaster University, and the Chair of Admissions for the Medical Sciences Graduate Program. His biomedical research focuses on understanding how chemical and environmental stresses during pregnancy affect the placenta and influence long-term health outcomes in babies. 
Dr. Raha is also the co-founder and Director of the McMaster Children and Youth University (MCYU), a community initiative that uses curiosity and creativity to break down barriers between youth and post-secondary education. Guided by the credo “Question, Discover, Create,” MCYU centers young voices through multidisciplinary, inquiry-based learning. Its research focuses on developing effective approaches to science communication and engaging youth as active research partners. Bruno Munari once wrote that he looked at what he was making and discovered that it functioned. Yacht designer Giorgio Cassetta has spent years unable to let that sentence go. We can explain structural, physical and mechanical function, but when a shape simply works we have no vocabulary for it. Drawing on research showing that rounded forms and the golden ratio trigger responses in the brain before any cognitive thought, and that abstract art instead divides even identical twins, he argues that part of aesthetic response is automatic and pre-cultural, and that it deserves serious study. title: When Design “Works”: Beyond Taste, Toward Objectivity | Giorgio Cassetta | TEDxForteDeiMarmi

description: You don't need a perfect plan to build a meaningful life or career. In this talk, CS Gagandeep Kaur Saluja shares how embracing uncertainty, making values-driven choices, and learning through experience can lead to unexpected opportunities and lasting success. Drawing from her journey in corporate governance, leadership, and social impact, she encourages audiences to stop waiting for certainty and start taking purposeful action because growth begins long before all the answers are known. CS Gagandeep Kaur Saluja is a Company Secretary, Corporate Governance Professional, and Legal & Compliance Expert currently associated with PwC. Passionate about ethical leadership and responsible governance, she mentors aspiring professionals and is the Founder of The Choice of Freedom, an initiative promoting personal growth and conscious living. title: “You Don’t Have to Have It All Figured Out” | Gagandeep Kaur Saluja | TEDxSAGEUniversity
